content.value_statement: Firebase sign-in setup can become inconsistent across providers and security rules. This skill gives focused guidance for Firebase Auth basics in AI coding sessions.
actual_capabilities: Explains Firebase Auth users, identity providers, ID tokens, and refresh tokens.
Shows setup paths through the Firebase CLI or Firebase Console.
Provides Web SDK guidance for email, OAuth, anonymous, and email-link sign-in.
Covers auth state observation and sign-out behavior for web apps.
Describes security rule checks using request.auth and owner matching.
limitations: Focuses on web SDK snippets and basic rules, not complete application architecture.
Does not provision Firebase resources automatically.
Some provider setup still requires Firebase Console configuration.
Does not replace threat modeling, production rule testing, or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Add web sign-in
use_cases.description: Plan email, OAuth, anonymous, or email-link sign-in for a Firebase web app.

use_cases.title: Protect user data
use_cases.description: Connect Firebase Authentication concepts to security rules that check signed-in users and ownership.

use_cases.title: Review auth flow
use_cases.description: Check whether a planned Firebase Auth flow covers provider setup, user state, and rule enforcement.

prompt_templates.title: Start email sign-in
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for email and password authentication.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add Firebase email and password sign-up and sign-in to my web app. Show the setup steps and explain required Firebase configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Add OAuth provider
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for a federated identity provider.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to configure Google sign-in for my Firebase web app. Include provider enablement, SDK setup, auth state handling, and sign-out behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Protect user-owned data
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate security rule planning for private user records.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design Firebase rules so users can read and write only their own profile documents. Include request.auth checks and ownership matching.

prompt_templates.title: Review auth design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a multi-provider authentication plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Firebase Auth plan for web, email links, OAuth, anonymous accounts, and rules. Identify gaps and safer defaults.

output_examples.input: I need Google and email sign-in for a React web app.
output_examples.output: A setup checklist covering Firebase prerequisites, provider enablement, SDK initialization, sign-in flows, auth-state handling, and sign-out behavior.

output_examples.input: Users should only access their own profile data.
output_examples.output: A rule design explanation that compares the signed-in user identifier with the profile identifier or owner field before allowing access.

output_examples.input: I want to test authentication locally before release.
output_examples.output: Guidance for connecting the web app to the Firebase Auth emulator during localhost development and switching to production configuration later.

best_practices: Enable only required providers and keep authorized redirect domains limited.
Use the Auth emulator during local development before production testing.
Write rules that verify request.auth and resource ownership for every protected path.
anti_patterns: Treating client-side auth state as the only access control.
Leaving broad read or write rules after adding sign-in.
Using placeholder redirect domains or sample URLs in production configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill create a Firebase project?
faq.answer: No. It explains prerequisites and setup paths. You still create and configure the project with Firebase tools or Console.

faq.question: Can it help with Google sign-in?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Google sign-in as a recommended provider and shows how provider setup fits the auth workflow.

faq.question: Does it cover mobile Auth SDKs?
faq.answer: No. The included SDK guidance focuses on web applications.

faq.question: Does it write complete security rules?
faq.answer: It covers auth-aware rule basics. Use dedicated Firestore or Storage guidance for complete production rules.

faq.question: Does it require the Firebase CLI?
faq.answer: No. The Firebase CLI is useful, but provider setup can also happen in the Firebase Console.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
